qs.q: Capsella is angiosperm because it possess -
qs.s: Angiosperms are flowering plants characterized by enclosed seeds within a fruit.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Which part of the reproductive structure produces both enzyme & hormone
qs.s: Tapetum produces enzymes like callase and hormones such as auxin (IAA) to nourish developing pollen grains.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Pro-ubisch bodies are produced in
qs.s: Pro-ubisch bodies are formed in the tapetum and later coated with sporopollenin to form Ubisch bodies.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Pollen grain represents
qs.s: Pollen grains represent the immature male gametophytic generation in angiosperms.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: A typical angiosperm anther contains
qs.s: A typical angiosperm anther is dithecous and tetrasporangiate, containing four microsporangia.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: How many cells or nuclei are present in mature male gametophyte of Capsella
qs.s: A mature male gametophyte consists of a 3-celled structure: one vegetative cell and two male gametes (or 3 nuclei).
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: How many and what type of male gametes are produced by the male gametophyte of Capsella
qs.s: Angiosperms produce two non-motile male gametes from the generative cell.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Ubisch bodies are associated with the development of
qs.s: Ubisch bodies help in the formation of the exine layer of pollen grains.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Pollen grain of Capsella is
qs.s: Dicot pollen grains, including Capsella, typically have three germ pores (tricolpate).
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Essential whorls of a flowers are
qs.s: Androecium and Gynoecium are essential whorls as they directly participate in sexual reproduction.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Sporopollenin is found in :-
qs.s: Sporopollenin forms the tough, resistant outer layer of pollen grains called the exine.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: In angiosperms, microsporophyll is known as:-
qs.s: The stamen is equivalent to the microsporophyll in angiosperms.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: In anther, main function of endothecium is:
qs.s: Fibrous thickenings in endothecium cells help in the dehiscence of the anther upon drying.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Which one is female gametophyte
qs.s: The embryo sac is the female gametophyte in angiosperms.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: The functional megaspore in Capsella is always
qs.s: In most angiosperms, the chalazal megaspore remains functional while the three micropylar ones degenerate.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Filiform apparatus are found in
qs.s: Filiform apparatus consists of finger-like projections found at the micropylar tip of synergids.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Perisperm is
qs.s: Perisperm is the residual, persistent nucellus present in certain seeds such as black pepper and beet.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: In angiosperms, megasporophyll is called :-
qs.s: The carpel or pistil is equivalent to the megasporophyll.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: How many pollen sacs are present in a mature anther at the time of dehiscence?
qs.s: At maturity, the partition between the two pollen sacs in each anther lobe dissolves, forming 2 large pollen sacs.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Anatropous (Resupinate) type of ovule is :-
qs.s: An anatropous ovule is completely inverted so that the micropyle lies close to the funicle.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: The special features of the endothecium of anther of Capsella :-
qs.s: Endothecium cells are radially elongated, have hygroscopic fibrous bands of alpha-cellulose, helping in dehiscence.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: When hilum, chalaza and micropyle lie in one straight line then ovule is called:
qs.s: An orthotropous ovule is straight, where micropyle, chalaza, and hilum lie in the same vertical line.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Pollen tube develops from
qs.s: The intine of the vegetative cell protrudes through a germ pore to form the pollen tube.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: 'Callase' enzyme which dissolves callose of tetrad of microspores to separate 4-microspores is secreted by:-
qs.s: Tapetum secretes callase enzyme which breaks down the callose wall surrounding microspore tetrads.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: The primary endosperm nucleus in Polygonum type of embryosac is :-
qs.s: Primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) is triploid (3n) as it results from triple fusion of a male gamete (n) and two polar nuclei (2n).
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Science of cultivation, breeding and marketing of flower is :-
qs.s: Floriculture is the branch of horticulture concerned with the cultivation and marketing of flowering plants.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: In Angioperms all the four microspores of tetrad are covered by a layer which is made up of :
qs.s: Microspores in a tetrad are initially held together and encased by a callose wall.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: All the nuclei in polygonum type of embryosac are
qs.s: All eight nuclei formed in a Polygonum-type embryo sac originate from mitotic divisions of a haploid megaspore, making them haploid.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: In which family pollinia are found:
qs.s: Pollen grains remain joined in compact masses called pollinia in Asclepiadaceae and Orchidaceae families.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Nucellus is found in :-
qs.s: Nucellus is the central tissue of the ovule containing nutrients for the developing embryo sac.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: The nutritive layer of microsporangia of Capsella is
qs.s: Tapetum is the innermost nutritive layer surrounding microspores.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: The haploid cell which divides by mitosis to form embryosac is :-
qs.s: The functional megaspore undergoes three successive mitotic divisions to form an 8-nucleate female gametophyte.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Microspore mother cell produces microspores by
qs.s: Microspore mother cells undergo meiotic division to produce haploid microspores.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Embryosac represents :-
qs.s: Embryo sac is the female gametophyte (megagametophyte) of flowering plants.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Pollen grains are able to withstand extremes of temperature and dessication because their exine is composed of :-
qs.s: Sporopollenin is one of the most resistant organic materials known, resisting chemical degradation and extreme heat.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: How many times flowering takes place in biennial plants :-
qs.s: Biennial plants complete their vegetative growth in the first year and flower once in the second year before dying.
qs.src: Conceptual - Male and Female Reproductive Organ

qs.q: Outer seed coat is known as :-
qs.s: The seed coat consists of an outer testa and an inner tegmen.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Which structure of the ovule is diploid :-
qs.s: Nucellus, integuments (maternal sporophytic tissues), and secondary nucleus (formed by fusion of two haploid polar nuclei) are all diploid.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Which type of growth is found in pollen tube :-
qs.s: Pollen tube elongation occurs strictly at its tip, known as apical tip growth.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: When pollen grains of a flower are transferred to stigma of another flower of a different plant, the process is called
qs.s: Transfer of pollen between flowers of two genetically distinct individual plants is called xenogamy.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Autogamy means
o: Transfer of pollen from anthers to stigma of the same flowers
Transfer of pollen from one flowers to another on the different plant
Occurence of male and female sex organ in the same flowers
qs.s: Autogamy refers to self-pollination within the same flower.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Maize is best example of :
qs.s: Maize produces abundant light pollen adapted for wind-pollination (anemophily).
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Which of the following promotes pollen germination and tube growth
qs.s: Boron is essential for sugar translocation and pollen tube growth.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Polyembryony was first discovered by
qs.s: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek discovered polyembryony in Citrus seeds in 1719.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Tegmen of the seed develops from:-
qs.s: The inner integument of the ovule forms the inner seed coat (tegmen).
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Example of Epihydrophily is :-
qs.s: In Vallisneria, female flowers reach the surface of water where pollination occurs (epihydrophily).
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Pollination in Yucca plant takes place by :-
qs.s: Yucca has an obligate symbiotic relation with the Pronuba moth (Tegeticula) for pollination.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: The main embryo is developed as a result of
o: Fusion of two polar nuclei of an embryosac
qs.s: Syngamy (fusion of male gamete with egg cell) forms the zygote which develops into the embryo.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: After fertilization the outer integument of ovule changes into -
qs.s: Outer integument transforms into the outer protective seed coat, the testa.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: After fertilization the seed is developed from
qs.s: The fertilized ovule matures into the seed.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Double fertilization means
o: Fusion of male gamete and ovum
A male gamete fused with egg and second male gamete fused with secondary nucleus
qs.s: Double fertilization involves syngamy and triple fusion within the embryo sac.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: After fertilization seed coat is formed by:
qs.s: Integuments of the ovule harden to form the seed coats.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: The product of fusion of secondary nucleus and male gamete is
qs.s: Fusion of a haploid male gamete with the diploid secondary nucleus forms the triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN).
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Water of coconut is
qs.s: Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: The suspensor in Capsella develops from
qs.s: The basal cell divides transversely to form a 6-10 celled suspensor.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Tigellum represents :-
qs.s: Tigellum is the main embryonal axis containing radicle and plumule.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: The number of haploid nuclei taking part in double fertilization are
qs.s: Five haploid nuclei participate: 1 egg nucleus + 2 male gamete nuclei + 2 polar nuclei.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: In albuminous seed, the food is stored in-
qs.s: Albuminous (endospermic) seeds retain endosperm as reserve food tissue.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Embryo of sunflower has :-
qs.s: Sunflower is a dicotyledonous plant, having two cotyledons in its embryo.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Endosperm is formed during the double fertilization by -
o: Two polar nuclei and one male gamete
One polar nuclei and one male gamete
Two polar nuclei and two male gametes
qs.s: Triple fusion between two polar nuclei and one male gamete generates endosperm.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Adventive embryony in Citrus is due to :
qs.s: In Citrus, nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac protrude into it and develop into embryos.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: In Angiosperms pollen tube liberates their male gametes into the :
qs.s: Pollen tube enters through a degenerating synergid and releases both male gametes into its cytoplasm.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: The aleurone layer in maize grain is specially rich in :-
qs.s: The outer proteinaceous layer of maize endosperm is called the aleurone layer.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Anthesis is a phenomenon which refers to-
qs.s: Anthesis is the process of opening of a flower bud to expose mature reproductive organs.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: When the pollens of one flower falls on the stigma of another flower of the same plant then genetically it is known as :-
qs.s: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically equivalent to autogamy as pollen comes from the same plant.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: What is the liquid part of green Coconut :-
qs.s: Liquid endosperm consists of free-nuclear endosperm tissue.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Entry of pollen tube through micropyle is called:
qs.s: Porogamy is the entry of the pollen tube into the ovule via the micropyle.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Through which cell of the embryosac, does the pollen tube enter the embryosac:
qs.s: The pollen tube enters the embryo sac through the degenerating synergid.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: Generally endosperm of angiosperm is :-
qs.s: Angiosperm endosperm is triploid (3n) due to triple fusion.
qs.src: Conceptual - Pollination, fertilization, endosperm, embryo, seed etc.

qs.q: What would be the number of chromosomes in the cells of the aleurone layer in a plant species with 8 chromosomes in its synergids ?
qs.s: Synergids are haploid (n=8). Aleurone layer is part of endosperm which is triploid (3n = 3 x 8 = 24).

qs.q: The arrangement of the nuclei in a normal embryosac in the dicot plants is
qs.s: Polygonum type embryo sac has 3 antipodals at chalazal end, 2 polar nuclei in central cell, and 3 cells in egg apparatus (3+2+3).

qs.q: In a Cereal grain the single cotyledon of embryo is represented by
qs.s: In grass/cereal embryos, the single shield-shaped cotyledon is called the scutellum.

qs.q: Long filamentous threads protruding at the end of a young cob of maize are:
qs.s: The silky threads of maize cob are long styles and stigmas that catch wind-borne pollen.

qs.q: In which of the following fruits is the edible part the aril ?
qs.s: Fleshy edible aril surrounding the seed is eaten in Litchi.

qs.q: Male gametes in angiosperms are formed by the division of :-
qs.s: The generative cell divides mitotically to form two male gametes.

qs.q: Which one of the following is surrounded by a callose wall ?
qs.s: Microspore mother cell undergoes callose wall formation during microsporogenesis.

qs.q: Unisexuality of flowers prevents :-
qs.s: Monoecious unisexual flowers prevent autogamy but allow geitonogamy.

qs.q: Endosperm is consumed by developing embryo in the seed of :-
qs.s: Pea has non-endospermic (exalbuminous) seeds where endosperm is completely consumed during development.

qs.q: Which one of the following is resistant to enzyme action?
qs.s: Exine is composed of sporopollenin, which cannot be degraded by any known enzyme.

qs.q: What does the filiform apparatus do at the entrance into ovule ?
o: It brings about opening of the pollen tube
It guides pollen tube from a synergid to egg
It helps in the entry of pollen tube into a synergid
It prevents entry of more than one pollen tube into the embryo sac
qs.s: Filiform apparatus secretes chemotropic substances that guide entry of pollen tube into synergid.

qs.q: Which one of the following pairs of plant structures has haploid number of chromosomes ?
o: Megaspore mother cell and antipodal cells
qs.s: Egg cell and antipodal cells are formed by megagametogenesis and are both haploid (n).

qs.q: An example of a seed with endosperm, perisperm, and caruncle is :-
qs.s: Castor seed possesses endosperm (food tissue), perisperm (persistent nucellus), and caruncle (integumentary outgrowth).

qs.q: The scutellum observed in a grain of wheat or maize is comparable to which part of the seed in other monocotyledons?
qs.s: Scutellum represents the single modified cotyledon in monocots.

qs.q: Apomictic embryos in citrus arise from:
qs.s: In Citrus, apomictic embryos develop from maternal sporophytic tissues like nucellus or integument.

qs.q: Wind pollinated flowers are:
o: Small, producing nectar and dry pollen
Small, brightly coloured, producing large number of pollen grains
Small, producing large number of dry pollen grains
Large, producing abundant nectar and pollen
qs.s: Anemophilous flowers produce small, light, dry, non-sticky pollen in large quantities.

qs.q: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant is called:
qs.s: Geitonogamy is transfer of pollen to stigma of another flower on same plant.

qs.q: What is common between vegetative reproduction and Apomixis ?
o: Both produces progeny identical to the parent.
Both are applicable to only dicot plants.
qs.s: Both vegetative reproduction and apomixis are asexual modes that produce genetically identical progeny (clones).

qs.q: In angiosperms, functional megaspore develops into :
qs.s: Functional megaspore develops into the female gametophyte (embryo sac).

qs.q: Filiform apparatus is a characteristic feature of :-
qs.s: Filiform apparatus is present at the micropylar end of synergid cells.

qs.q: Nucellar polyembryony is reported in species of :-
qs.s: Nucellar adventive embryony is characteristic of Citrus species.

qs.q: In which one of the following pollination is autogamous ?
qs.s: Cleistogamous flowers never open, ensuring strict autogamy.

qs.q: What would be the number of chromosomes of the aleurone cells of a plant with 42 chromosomes in its root tip cells ?
qs.s: Root tip cells are diploid (2n=42 => n=21). Aleurone cells are triploid (3n = 3 x 21 = 63).

qs.q: The coconut water and the edible part of coconut are equivalent to :-
qs.s: Both liquid coconut water and solid white kernel are endosperm tissue.

qs.q: The gynoecium consists of many free pistils in flowers of :-
qs.s: Michelia has a polycarpellary apocarpous (free pistils) gynoecium.

qs.q: Both, autogamy and geitonogamy are prevented in:-
qs.s: Papaya is dioecious (male and female flowers on distinct plants), preventing both autogamy and geitonogamy.

qs.q: Even in absence of pollinating agents seed-setting is assured in :-
qs.s: Commelina possesses cleistogamous flowers which self-pollinate without external agents.

qs.q: Plants with ovaries having only one or a few ovules, are generally pollinated by :-
qs.s: Anemophilous (wind-pollinated) plants usually have single-ovoled ovaries.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
o: Pollen grains in some plants remain viable for months.
Intine is made up of cellulose and pectin.
When pollen is shed at two celled stage, double fertilization does not take place.
Vegetative cell is larger than generative cell.
qs.s: In 60% angiosperms, pollen is shed at 2-celled stage; generative cell divides later in the pollen tube, so double fertilization still occurs.

qs.q: What is the function of germ pore?
o: Absorption of water for seed germination
qs.s: Germ pores are exine apertures where sporopollenin is absent, allowing pollen tube initiation.

qs.q: Perisperm differs from endosperm in:
o: Its formation by fusion of secondary nucleus with several sperms
qs.s: Perisperm is persistent diploid nucellar tissue, whereas endosperm is triploid.

qs.q: Megasporangium is equivalent to:
qs.s: The ovule of an angiosperm is equivalent to an integumented megasporangium.

qs.q: Advantage of cleistogamy is :-
qs.s: Cleistogamous flowers assure seed setting even without pollinating agents.

qs.q: Seed coat is not thin, membranous in:
qs.s: Coconut has a hard woody endocarp, while its seed coat is merged; in options like gram/maize/groundnut it is thin membranous.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Hard outer layer of pollen is called intine
qs.s: Tapetum is the innermost microsporangial wall layer that nourishes pollen grains.

qs.q: Geitonogamy involves:
o: fertilization of a flower by the pollen from another flower of the same plant.
fertilization of a flower by the pollen from the same flower.
fertilization of a flower by the pollen from a flower of another plant in the same population.
fertilization of a flower by the pollen from a flower of another plant belonging to a distant population.
qs.s: Geitonogamy is pollination between two different flowers borne on the same plant.

qs.q: Male gametophyte with least number of cell is present in:
qs.s: In angiosperms (Lilium), male gametophyte is reduced to 3 cells (1 vegetative + 2 male gametes).

qs.q: Pollen tablets are available in the market for:
qs.s: Pollen grains are rich in nutrients and consumed as food supplements (tablets/syrups).

qs.q: Function of filiform apparatus is to :-
o: Recognize the suitable pollen at stigma
Guide the entry of pollen tube
qs.s: Filiform apparatus directs pollen tube growth into the synergid.

qs.q: Non-albuminous seed is produced in :-
qs.s: Pea seeds consume their endosperm completely before seed maturation.

qs.q: Transmission tissue is characteristic feature of :-
qs.s: Solid styles possess specialized central transmission tissue through which pollen tubes grow.

qs.q: Which one of the following may require pollinators, but is genetically similar to autogamy ?
qs.s: Geitonogamy requires agents to transfer pollen between flowers, but both flowers belong to same genetic individual.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is not true?
o: Pollen grains of some plants cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people
The flowers pollinated by flies and bats secrete foul odour to attract them
Honey is made by bees by digesting - pollen collected from flowers
Pollen grains are rich in nutrients, and they are used in the form of tablets and syrups
qs.s: Source key: option 3. Honey is made by bees from floral nectar, not by digesting pollen grains.

qs.q: The hilum is a scar on the :
o: Fruit, where it was attached to pedicel
qs.s: Hilum is the scar on a seed coat representing the point of attachment to the stalk (funicle).

qs.q: Which of the following are the important floral rewards to the animal pollinators?
qs.s: Nectar and edible pollen grains serve as natural food rewards for pollinators.

qs.q: Male gametophyte in angiosperms produces:
o: Two sperms and a vegetative cell
Single sperm and a vegetative cell
Single sperm and two vegetative cells
qs.s: A mature angiosperm male gametophyte comprises 3 cells: 2 non-motile male gametes (sperms) and 1 vegetative cell.

qs.q: Coconut water from a tender coconut is:
o: Innermost layers of the seed coat
qs.s: Liquid endosperm of tender coconut consists of thousands of free nuclei.

qs.q: Filiform apparatus is characteristic feature of:
qs.s: Filiform apparatus is located in synergids of the egg apparatus.

qs.q: The wheat grain has an embryo with one large, shield-shaped cotyledon known as:
qs.s: The single cotyledon of grass/cereal grains is called scutellum.

qs.q: Which one of the following fruits is parthenocarpic?
qs.s: Banana develops seedless fruits without fertilization (parthenocarpy).

qs.q: In angiosperms, microsporogenesis and megasporogenesis:
qs.s: Both processes involve meiotic division of sporocyte cells to form haploid spores.

qs.q: Flowers are unisexual in:
qs.s: Cucumber bears unisexual flowers on the same plant (monoecious).

qs.q: The coconut water from tender coconut represents:-
qs.s: Coconut water is liquid free-nuclear endosperm tissue.

qs.q: Proximal end of the filament of stamen is attached to the
qs.s: The proximal end of the stamen filament attaches to the thalamus or petal of the flower.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is not true?
o: Tapetum helps in the dehiscence of anther
Exine of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin
Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies
Stored pollen in liquid nitrogen can be used in the crop breeding programmes
qs.s: Tapetum provides nutrition; dehiscence is facilitated by the endothecium.

qs.q: Cotyledon of maize grain is called :-
qs.s: The cotyledon of maize grain is named scutellum.

qs.q: Seed formation without fertilization in flowering plants involves the process of :-
qs.s: Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction by producing seeds without fertilization.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
o: Pollen grains of many species can germinate on the stigma of a flower, but only one pollen tube of the same species grows into the style.
Insects that consume pollen or nectar without bringing about pollination are called pollen/nectar robbers.
Pollen germination and pollen tube growth are regulated by chemical components of pollen interacting with those of the pistil.
Some reptiles have also been reported as pollinators in some plant species.
qs.s: Multiple pollen grains of the compatible species can germinate and send pollen tubes down the style.

qs.q: Which one of the following generates new genetic combinations leading to variation ?
qs.s: Sexual reproduction creates genetic variation due to meiotic crossing over and random fertilization.

qs.q: In majority of angiosperms:
o: Reduction division occurs in the megaspore mother cells
A small central cell is present in the embryo sac
qs.s: Megaspore mother cell undergoes reductional division (meiosis) to produce haploid megaspores.

qs.q: Pollination in water hyacinth and water lily is brought about by the agency of:
qs.s: Water hyacinth and water lily emergent flowers reach above water surface and are pollinated by insects or wind.

qs.q: The ovule of an angiosperm is technically equivalent to:
qs.s: An ovule is equivalent to an integumented megasporangium.

qs.q:
Match column-I with column-II and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I
(a) Pistils fused together
(b) Formation of gametes
(c) Hyphae of higher Ascomycetes
(d) Unisexual female flower
Column-II
(i) Gametogenesis
(ii) Pistillate
(iii) Syncarpous
(iv) Dikaryotic
Select the correct option:
qs.s: Fused pistils = Syncarpous; Gamete formation = Gametogenesis; Ascomycetes hyphae = Dikaryotic; Female flower = Pistillate.

qs.q: Functional megaspore in an angiosperm develops into ?
qs.s: The functional megaspore undergoes mitoses to form the embryo sac.

qs.q: Attractants and rewards are required for :
qs.s: Insect-pollinated flowers (entomophily) require nectar and pollen rewards along with color/fragrance attractants.

qs.q: Plants which produce characteristic pneumatophores and show vivipary belong to:
qs.s: Halophytes (mangroves) possess respiratory roots (pneumatophores) and exhibit vivipary.

qs.q: Flowers which have single ovule in the ovary and are packed into inflorescence are usually pollinated by:
qs.s: Wind-pollinated plants often have single-ovoled ovaries clustered in dense inflorescences.

qs.q: A dioecious flowering plant prevents both :
qs.s: Dioecious plants have male and female flowers on separate individuals, preventing autogamy and geitonogamy.

qs.q: Double fertilization is exhibited by:
qs.s: Double fertilization is a unique diagnostic feature of angiosperms.

qs.q: Which of the following flowers only once in its life-time ?
qs.s: Bamboo species are monocarpic plants that flower once in 50-100 years and then die.

qs.q: Pollen grains can be stored for several years in liquid nitrogen having a temperature of
qs.s: Cryopreservation of pollen grains is performed in liquid nitrogen at -196°C.

qs.q: Double fertilization is
o: Fusion of two male gametes of a pollen tube with two different eggs
Fusion of one male gamete with two polar nuclei
Fusion of two male gametes with one egg
qs.s: Double fertilization consists of two events: syngamy (fertilization) and triple fusion.

qs.q: Which one of the following plants shows a very close relationship with a species of moth, where none of the two can complete its life cycle without the other?
qs.s: Yucca and Pronuba moth share an obligate mutualistic relationship.

qs.q: In some plants, the female gamete develops into embryo without fertilization. This phenomenon is known as:
qs.s: Parthenogenesis is the development of an unfertilized egg into an embryo.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements regarding post-fertilization development in flowering plants is incorrect?
qs.s: Ovules develop into seeds after fertilization, not into embryo sacs.

qs.q: Persistent nucellus in the seed is known as:
qs.s: Perisperm is residual persistent nucellus in seeds.

qs.q: What is the fate of the male gametes discharged in the synergid?
o: One fuses with the egg, other(s) degenerate(s) in the synergid.
One fuses with the egg, other(s) fuse(s) with synergid nucleus.
One fuses with the egg and other fuses with central cell nuclei.
qs.s: One male gamete fuses with the egg nucleus (syngamy), and the other fuses with the secondary nucleus in central cell (triple fusion).

qs.q: Which is the most common type of embryo sac in angiosperms ?
o: Tetrasporic with one mitotic stage of divisions
Monosporic with three sequential mitotic divisions
Monosporic with two sequential mitotic divisions
Bisporic with two sequential mitotic divisions
qs.s: Polygonum type embryo sac is monosporic and requires 3 sequential mitotic divisions to form 8 nuclei.

qs.q: What type of pollination takes place in Vallisneria?
o: Pollination occurs in submerged condition by water
Flowers emerge above surface of water, and pollination occurs by insects.
Flowers emerge above water surface, and pollen is carried by wind.
Male flowers are carried by water currents to female flowers at surface of water
qs.s: Female flowers float on surface via long stalks; detached male flowers drift passively on surface to meet them.

qs.q: In which one of the following, both autogamy and geitonogamy are prevented?
qs.s: Papaya is dioecious, preventing both autogamy and geitonogamy.

qs.q: In water hyacinth and water lily, pollination takes place by:
qs.s: Their flowers emerge above water surface and are pollinated by insects or wind.

qs.q: The body of the ovule is fused within the funicle at:
qs.s: Hilum is the point of attachment/fusion between ovule body and funicle.

qs.q:
The plant parts which consist of two generations one within the other:
(a) Pollen grains inside the anther
(b) Germinated pollen grain with two male gametes
(c) Seed inside the fruit
(d) Embryo sac inside the ovule
qs.s: Pollen grains (gametophyte, n) reside inside anther (sporophyte, 2n) and embryo sac (n) inside ovule (2n).

qs.q: Which of the following is incorrect for wind -pollinated plants ?
o: Flowers are small and not brightly coloured
Pollen grains are light and non-sticky
qs.s: Wind-pollinated plants generally have a single ovule in each ovary.

qs.q: Vegetative propagules in Agave is termed as:
qs.s: Agave reproduces vegetatively through fleshy floral buds called bulbils.

qs.q: Male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free living existence in :-
qs.s: In seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms), gametophytes remain retained on the sporophyte.

qs.q: The term used for transfer of pollen grains from anthers of one plant to stigma of a different plant which, during pollination, brings genetically different types of pollen grains to stigma, is:
qs.s: Xenogamy introduces genetically different pollen onto the stigma.

qs.q: A typical angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is:
qs.s: The Polygonum type mature embryo sac contains 7 cells and 8 nuclei.

qs.q: In some members of which of the following pairs of families, pollen grains retain their viability for months after release ?
qs.s: Members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae maintain pollen viability for months.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
(a) The ovule is attached to the placenta by means of a stalk called hilum.
(b) Funicle represents the junction between ovule and hilum.
(c) Each ovule has one or two protective envelopes called integuments.
(d) A small opening is present at the tip of ovule called micropyle.
qs.s: Stalk is called funicle; junction between funicle and ovule is hilum. Thus (a) and (b) are false; (c) and (d) are true.

qs.q: Which of the following plants are pollinated by water?
qs.s: Hydrilla, Zostera, and Vallisneria are classic hydrostatical water-pollinated plants.

qs.q: Product of asexual reproduction generally generates
o: Offspring that are exact copies of their parent
qs.s: Asexual reproduction produces clones that are genetically and morphologically identical.

qs.q: Identify the incorrect statement related to Pollination:
o: Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollination
Flowers produce foul odours to attract flies and beetles to get pollinated
Moths and butterflies are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects
Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants
qs.s: Bees are the most dominant biotic pollinating agents among insects, not moths/butterflies.

qs.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous
Statement II: Cleistogamy is disadvantageous as there is no chance for cross pollination.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
qs.s: Cleistogamous flowers never open so they are strictly autogamous; lack of cross-pollination limits variation.

qs.q: Which part of the fruit, labelled in the given figure makes it a false fruit?
qs.alt: Diagram showing cross section of apple with labels A, B, C, D.
qs.s: Label C represents the swollen edible thalamus of apple which forms the flesh of false fruit.

qs.q: What will be the ploidy of endosperm of a seed produced after crossing tetraploid female plant with tetraploid male plant?
qs.s: Female tetraploid (4n) produces 2n egg and 4n central cell (2 polar nuclei of 2n each). Male (4n) gives 2n gamete. Endosperm = 4n + 2n = 6n (hexaploid).

qs.q: Which of the following set represents the correct labelling of A, B, C and D with respect to the given diagram?
qs.alt: Seed diagram with labels A, B, C, D.
qs.s: A is seed coat, B is cotyledon, C is endosperm, and D is hypocotyl.

qs.q: In general the egg apparatus of embryo sac in angiosperm consists of:
o: One egg cell, two synergids, three antipodal cells, two Polar nuclei
One egg cell, two synergids, two antipodal cells, three Polar nuclei
One egg cell, three synergids, two antipodal cells, two Polar nuclei
One egg cell, two synergids, two antipodal cells, two Polar nuclei
qs.s: Egg apparatus specifically consists of 1 egg cell + 2 synergids. Option 1 represents complete female gametophyte structure as keyed.

qs.q: The residual persistent part which forms the perisperm in the seeds of beet is:
qs.s: Persistent residual nucellus in seeds like beet forms perisperm.

qs.q: Which of the following can be expected if scientists succeed in introducing apomictic gene into hybrid varieties of crops ?
o: Polyembryony will be seen and each seed will produce many plantlets
Seeds of hybrid plants will show longer dormancy
Farmers can keep on using the seeds produced by the hybrids to raise new crop year after year
There will be segregation of the desired characters only in the progeny
qs.s: Apomixis prevents segregation of hybrid traits, allowing farmers to reuse hybrid seeds continuously.

qs.q: Each cell of sporogenous tissue is potential pollen or microspore mother cell; Division taking place in sporogenous cell is :-
qs.s: Sporogenous cells undergo reductional division (meiosis) to form microspores.

qs.q: In over 60% of angiosperms pollen grains are shed at :-
qs.s: In 60% of angiosperms, pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage (vegetative cell and generative cell).

qs.q: Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies & bronchial afflictions in some people often leading to chronic respiratory disorder such as :-
qs.s: Pollen allergen exposure can induce both asthma and bronchitis.

qs.q: In a pollen grain the small cell is spindle shaped with dense cytoplasm is :-
qs.s: Generative cell is small, spindle-shaped, and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell.

qs.q: The innermost wall layer of anther is tapetum; the main function of tapetum is :-
qs.s: Tapetum provides essential nutrients to developing microspores.

qs.q: Two non motile male gametes in angiosperms are produced by :-
qs.s: Generative cell divides mitotically to produce two non-motile male gametes.

qs.q: Which of the following haploid structure is present in male plant of papaya?
qs.s: Generative cell is haploid (n), while microspore mother cells are diploid and antipodals exist in female plants.

qs.q: Pollen grain represents
qs.s: Pollen grain is the male gametophyte of angiosperms.

qs.q: A typical angiosperm embryosac at maturity is :-
qs.s: Mature female gametophyte has 7 cells containing 8 nuclei.

qs.q: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of same plant is called :-
qs.s: Pollination between different flowers of the same plant is geitonogamy.

qs.q: The part of pistil which acts as landing platform for pollen grain is :-
qs.s: Stigma serves as the receptive surface for pollen grains.

qs.q: Non albuminous seeds are present in :-
qs.s: Both pea and groundnut seeds are non-albuminous (exalbuminous).

qs.q: The type of cells under going meiosis in the flowers are
o: Microspore mother cells & megaspore mother cell
qs.s: Sporocytes (PMC and MMC) undergo meiotic divisions.

qs.q: Chasmocleistogamous flowers are present in :-
qs.s: Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina produce both chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers.

qs.q: Although in most of species fruits are result of fertilisation, there are a few species in which fruit develops without fertilisation - process is known as:
qs.s: Fruit formation without fertilization is called parthenocarpy.

qs.q: One of the male gamete moves towards the egg cell & fuses with it, the process is known as :-
qs.s: Fusion of a male gamete with the egg cell nucleus is syngamy.

qs.q: Nucellar polyembryony is reported in species of :-
qs.s: Nucellar polyembryony occurs commonly in both Citrus and Mango.

qs.q: Which of the following are crucial for the storage of seeds ?
qs.s: Dehydration and dormancy allow seeds to stay viable during storage.

qs.q: The function of suspensor is
o: To push the embryo towards endosperm to provide more food
qs.s: Suspensor elongates to push the developing embryo deeper into the endosperm for nutrition.

qs.q: Single shield shaped cotyledon of grass is known as:-
qs.s: Scutellum is the modified single cotyledon of grass embryo.

qs.q: Epicotyl has a shoot apex and few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure known as :-
qs.s: Coleoptile is the protective sheath covering the epicotyl and shoot apex in monocots.

qs.q: Micropyle in seed helps in the entry of
qs.s: During seed germination, micropyle facilitates entry of water and oxygen.

qs.q: The coconut water from tender coconut that you are familiar with is :-
qs.s: Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm.

qs.q: Endosperm development precedes embryo development, the endosperm of angiospermic plant is :-
qs.s: Endosperm in angiosperms is a triploid (3n) nutritive tissue.

qs.q: Which of the following structure is not present in embryo of gram
qs.s: Coleoptile is found only in monocot embryos, whereas gram is a dicot.

qs.q: The portion of embryonal axis below the level of cotyledon is known as :-
qs.s: Hypocotyl is the portion of embryonal axis below the level of cotyledons terminating in radicle.

qs.q: In some seeds, remnant of nucellus is known as :-
qs.s: Persistent remnant of nucellus in seed is perisperm.

qs.q: Perisperm is present in:
qs.s: Both beet and black pepper retain perisperm in mature seeds.

qs.q: Seeds are produced without fertilization in some members of
qs.s: Apomictic seed formation is common in Asteraceae and grasses.

qs.q: Parthenogenesis occurs when :-
o: Embryo is formed without the fusion of egg and sperm (male gamete)
Embryo is formed by the fusion of egg and sperm
Embryo is formed from nucellar cell
qs.s: Parthenogenesis is development of an embryo directly from an unfertilized egg cell.

qs.q: In a type of apomixis which is known as adventive embryony, embryos develop directly from the :
o: Synergids or antipodals of an embryosac
qs.s: Adventive embryos arise directly from diploid sporophytic tissues like nucellus or integuments.

qs.q: Proliferation of integumentary cells at the micropylar region of the ovule in castor develops
qs.s: Caruncle is a fleshy outgrowth produced from the outer integument at micropyle in castor seed.

qs.q: Just before fertilization the diploid structure in the ovule of Capsella is
qs.s: Both nucellus and secondary nucleus (formed by polar nuclei fusion) are diploid.

qs.q: Free nuclear division in an angiosperm takes place during
qs.s: Nuclear endosperm development involves initial free nuclear divisions without cell wall formation.

qs.q: Protandry is the situation when :-
o: Anther matures later than the stigma of flower
Anther matures earlier than the stigma of flower
Anther and stigma mature at the same time
qs.s: Protandry is dichogamy where anthers mature and shed pollen before stigma becomes receptive.

qs.q: The anterior end of pollen tube burst by the process of in embryosac-
qs.s: Pollen tube tip absorbs water (endosmosis) in synergid cytoplasm and bursts open.

qs.q: In angiosperms haploid, diploid and triploid conditions respectively can be traced in :-
qs.s: Egg cell is haploid (n), nucellus is diploid (2n), and endosperm is triploid (3n).

qs.q: If the leaf of Capsella has 46 number of chromosomes then how many chromosomes number will be there in endosperm -
qs.s: Leaf is diploid (2n=46 => n=23). Endosperm is triploid (3n = 3 x 23 = 69).

qs.q: If the nucellus cell of an Angiosperm contains 24 chromosomes, the number of chromosomes present in pollen grain, endosperm & embryo will be
qs.s: Nucellus (2n=24 => n=12). Pollen grain (n=12), endosperm (3n=36), embryo (2n=24).

qs.q: In Angiosperm, if haploid number of chromosome is 12 then what will be the no. of chromosomes in integuments and synergids :-
qs.s: Integuments are diploid (2n = 2 x 12 = 24); synergids are haploid (n = 12).

qs.q: In Angiosperm, if number of chromosomes in endosperm is 30, what will be the no. of chromosomes in nucellus :-
qs.s: Endosperm is 3n=30 => n=10. Nucellus is diploid (2n = 20).

qs.q: How many meiotic divisions are necessary for the formation of 100 functional megaspores:-
qs.s: Each meiotic division of a megaspore mother cell produces 1 functional megaspore (3 degenerate). Thus 100 meiosis are needed.

qs.q: The seeds of which type of plant have no dormancy
qs.s: Mangrove seeds show vivipary where seeds germinate while attached to mother plant without dormancy.

qs.q: Anemophily type of pollination is found in:
qs.s: Coconut palms are anemophilous (wind-pollinated) angiosperms.

qs.q: In grass what happens in microspore mother cell for the formation of mature pollen grain:
o: One meiotic and two mitotic divisions
One meiotic and one mitotic division
qs.s: MMC undergoes 1 meiotic division to form microspores, followed by 1 mitotic division to form 2-celled pollen grain.

qs.q: Syncarpous gynoecium is found in :-
qs.s: Papaver possesses a polycarpellary syncarpous gynoecium.

qs.q: When a diploid female plant is crossed with a tetraploid male plant, the ploidy of endosperm cells in the resulting seed will be :-
qs.s: Diploid female gives 2 polar nuclei (n+n = 2n total). Tetraploid male gives 2n male gamete. Endosperm = 2n + 2n = 4n (tetraploid).

qs.q: If diploid female plant is crossed with tetra ploid male plant. What would be ploidy level of seed coat.
qs.s: Seed coat develops from maternal integuments which remain diploid (2n).

qs.q: Perispermic and endospermic seeds are found in
qs.s: Castor seed has both prominent endosperm and perisperm.

qs.q: Double fertilization involves :-
o: Fertilization of the egg by two male gametes
Fertilization of two eggs in the same embryosac by two sperms brought by one pollen tube
Fertilization of the egg and the central cell by two sperms (male gametes) brought by different pollen tubes
Fertilization of the egg and the central cell by two sperms (male gametes) brought by the same pollen tube
qs.s: One pollen tube releases two male gametes into synergid: one fertilizes the egg cell (syngamy) and the other fertilizes the central cell (triple fusion).
